title: Renal failure flowchart, RPRF causes & RPGN features
guide: Renal failure divides into CKD and non-CKD; non-CKD splits by speed into AKI (hours–days) and RPRF (days–weeks). RPRF is caused by RPGN (glomerular pathology), HUS, severe acute interstitial nephritis and (some cases of) atheroembolic renal disease. RPGN itself = RPRF + diffuse proliferative GN with crescents. Learn the urine protein, oedema compartment and the laboratory panel.

title: RPGN biopsy: crescents, IF patterns and the dialysis-first rule
guide: Light microscopy: parietal epithelial proliferation with fibrin crescents (number matters). Immunofluorescence: negative, diffuse granular, linear and granular panels — linear IF marking type I RPGN, with associations Goodpasture disease (linear), diabetes mellitus and light chain disease (granular). Never biopsy a markedly raised creatinine at once: dialyse, recheck and only then biopsy.

title: RPGN treatment approach, dialysis indications & types I–V
guide: Step 1 checks: ECG (hyperkalaemia → calcium gluconate 10 mL IV over 2–3 min), ABG (metabolic acidosis → NaHCO₃ or dialysis) and volume status (IVC diameter → diuretics). Absolute dialysis indications are uremic; relative ones are resistant volume overload, hyperkalaemia and acidosis. IF-based types: I Goodpasture (linear), II immune complex (<20 years, SLE most important), III pauci-immune (commonest), plus the double-positive type IV (good prognosis) versus double-negative type V (poor prognosis) table.

title: Pulmonary renal syndrome, Goodpasture HLA and dialysis disequilibrium
guide: Pulmonary renal syndrome = RPGN + diffuse alveolar haemorrhage; list Goodpasture, microscopic polyangiitis, granulomatosis with polyangiitis and active SLE. Goodpasture disease targets the noncollagenous domain of the α3 chain of type-IV collagen with triggers smoking, hydrocarbons, fluid overload and lung infection; DR2/15 and DR4 are high risk, DR1 and DR7 low risk. Dialysis disequilibrium: first session <1 hour, subsequent 4 hours, else ↓osmolality drives water into cells → cerebral oedema, seizure, death.

title: Goodpasture presentation, work-up, treatment and post-transplant notes
guide: Lung involvement in 75% with cough, haemoptysis, smoking history and no fever; renal involvement means poor prognosis. DLCO is increased, X-ray shows B/L diffuse infiltrate and CT shows diffuse alveolar haemorrhage. Active management for ongoing pulmonary haemorrhage, creatinine <5.5 mg/dL with normal urine output, new cellular crescent and type IV RPGN; mainstay PLEX + steroid/cyclophosphamide for 3–6 months; transplant after 6 months of antibody negativity. Goodpasture does not recur post-transplant, whereas Alport syndrome carries a 5% risk of post-transplant Goodpasture syndrome.
